sources.title: Motor adaptation scaled by the difficulty of a secondary cognitive task
Closed-Loop Task Difficulty Adaptation during Virtual Reality Reach-to-Grasp Training Assisted with an Exoskeleton for Stroke Rehabilitation
sources.authors: Grimm F, Naros G, Gharabaghi A.

sources.title: Enhancing generalisation in biofeedback intervention using the challenge point framework: a case study
Self-adaptive over progressive non-adaptive immersive virtual reality serious game to promote motor learning in older adults - A double blind randomized controlled trial
sources.authors: Everard G, Vermette M, Dumas-Longpré E, Hoang T, Robitaille M, Sorrentino G, Edwards MG, Lejeune T, Batcho CS.

findings.finding: Motor adaptation is impaired when the executive system is heavily burdened by a difficult secondary task.
findings.quote: We find that motor adaptation was specifically impaired on the most difficult to categorize trials.

findings.finding: Adjusting task difficulty with an adaptation algorithm improves movement accuracy, velocity, and range of motion.
findings.quote: The level of difficulty for the exercise was adjusted by a performance-dependent real-time adaptation algorithm.

findings.finding: Adjusting treatment difficulty based on performance criteria helps learners generalise their skills beyond basic levels.
findings.quote: Treatment difficulty was adjusted in an adaptive manner following predetermined criteria for advancing, maintaining, or moving back a level

findings.finding: Self-adaptive serious games that dynamically adjust to individual performance lead to greater improvements in speed-accuracy trade-offs.
findings.quote: Self-adaptive serious games, which dynamically adjust task difficulty, may provide additional benefits by tailoring challenges to individual performance.

principle: Adjusting task difficulty dynamically based on performance helps learners improve their movements and generalise their skills.
for_the_teacher: Dynamically adjust the difficulty of the movement practice based on how well the learner is performing in real time.
